title: The tawaf of Ifadah

lines: IS SHE GOING TO HOLD US UP?
cards: The Hajj is nearly over, and the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is told that Safiyyah, one of his wives, has started her period. His first question is practical: is she going to hold us up? Will the whole party have to wait for her?
Then a second question. Did she already do the tawaf, the circling of the Ka'ba, after the day of sacrifice? Yes, they tell him, she did.
Then, he says, let's go. One question decided whether everyone waited. Today, the tawaf of Ifadah.

teach.h: UP TO MECCA, AFTER THE SACRIFICE.
teach.b: First, where it falls. The pilgrims have stood at Arafah, slept at Muzdalifah, thrown the stones, offered the sacrifice and cut their hair. Then they go up to Mecca.

Jabir's account in Sahih Muslim says the Prophet rode to the House, circled it, and prayed zuhr in Mecca. Then he came to his own clan as they drew water from Zamzam, and drank. Second, the Qur'an's line for it.
In Surah Al-Hajj, after the sacrifice, pilgrims are told to finish their unkempt state, fulfill their vows, and "go around the ancient House." Commentators connect that line to this circling.
Tradition counts it among the pillars of Hajj, the parts without which the Hajj isn't complete. Some other rites, if missed, can be made up with an offering. This one has to be done.
That's the weight behind Safiyyah's story: his question suggests the whole party would have waited for it, and once he heard it was done, nothing else stood in the way. Fourth, what it finishes.
With this circling, and the walk between Safa and Marwa for those who still owe it, the last restrictions of ihram lift.

The pilgrim who arrived at the boundary in two white cloths is now, in the eyes of the law, free. One more circling comes at the very end, but that belongs to a later day. Today's is the one the Hajj stands on.
After all the big, open places, the plain, the valley, the pillars, the journey comes back to the same small center it started from, and goes around it again.

how: After the stoning, sacrifice and haircut, pilgrims go to Mecca and circle the Ka'ba in the tawaf of Ifadah, a required pillar of Hajj, often followed by the walk between Safa and Marwa.

games.q: what does “the tawaf of ifadah” mean?
o: the circling after the sacrifice that every Hajj needs
the last circling before a pilgrim leaves Mecca
the first circling when a pilgrim reaches Mecca

games.q: the tawaf of ifadah — tap the pairs.
p: is she going to hold us up?
what Surah Al-Hajj says to go around
the prayer he prayed in Mecca that day

s: the tawaf of Ifadah can be skipped if a pilgrim is tired
tradition counts it among the pillars of Hajj; without it the Hajj isn't complete.
the Prophet would have waited for Safiyyah if she hadn't done it
his question, will she hold us up, shows the party would have had to wait.
it comes after Arafah, Muzdalifah, the stoning and the sacrifice.

games.q: you're traveling with the Prophet's household at the end of Hajj. Safiyyah has started her period. what decides whether everyone waits?
o: whether she has already done the tawaf after the day of sacrifice.
games.why: told she had already circled the House, the Prophet says let's go.

practice: Bring to mind something you've nearly finished: a letter that only needs signing, a repair that needs one more screw. Find the last step, the one the whole thing stands on, and see yourself doing it slowly, all the way to the end.
If you pray, ask for help finishing it; if not, let the finished version rest in your mind.

wordCard.voice: The tawaf of Ifadah. The circling of the Ka'ba after Arafah and the day of sacrifice, a pillar of Hajj that has to be done. Today's word.

orig.note: the circling done after pilgrims come back from Arafah and Mina.

carryVoice: Your line: the essential circling. Some steps can be made up; this one carries the rest. Go gently.
